subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary from our call:
- You’re evaluating inference for real-time fraud scoring in your payments flow.
- Primary SLO is 99th percentile latency under 150ms for single-request scoring.
- Expected steady-state: ~1k QPS across peak windows, with bursts to ~3–5k for promotions.
- Data residency: US-only, but not strictly on-prem (cloud VPC acceptable).

Initial recommendation:
- Given the latency + burst profile and the need for predictable throughput, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) is the best fit. Dedicated gives you predictable tail latency and isolated capacity during bursts. Hosted API can work for PoCs or very low sustained QPS, but it will be harder to guarantee the P99 under big bursts without reserved capacity.

Concrete next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected sustained QPS vs peak burst QPS and the percent of requests that must hit <=150ms P99? (Simple numbers will do.)
2) Any procurement constraints or preferred term length for reserved capacity (monthly vs annual)?
3) I’ve attached a short cheatsheet on latency/throughput tradeoffs and a draft SOW for Dedicated — Connor is looping in for pricing.

If it helps, I can put together a short benchmarking plan (2–3 day test) to validate P99 latency for your typical payload.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf), latency-throughput-cheatsheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alex Morgan <alex@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap. A few answers and one quick question: 

Answers:
- Steady-state: ~1k QPS (mostly daytime US East), expected to grow ~30% over 12 months.
- Peak bursts: 3.5k–5k QPS for 10–30 minute windows during marketing spikes.
- Latency requirement: ~95% of requests can be tolerant up to 100ms; but we need the P99 <= 150ms for risk scoring to avoid checkout friction.
- Procurement: we prefer annual commits but need to see pricing and SLA tiers before committing.

Question:
- How big a difference in unit cost do you typically see between Hosted API at high volume vs Dedicated capacity? We need a high-level sense for business case to take to finance.

Also looping in our infra lead, Sana, for any VPC/networking questions.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, FinTechCo
alex@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Sana Iqbal <sana@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Alex — that aligns with what we discussed. Two quick notes on the cost/SLA question and proposed next steps: 

Cost delta (high-level):
- Hosted API: simpler (pay-as-you-go) but unit token/compute cost at sustained high QPS typically 1.8–2.5x higher than well-utilized Dedicated, depending on your batching profile and model selection. Hosted is great for ramp/PoC and unpredictable workloads.
- Dedicated: higher upfront commit but much lower marginal cost at scale. If you can commit annually and sustain steady-state ~1k QPS with expected growth, Dedicated usually becomes cost-efficient by month 3–6 for heavy inference workloads.
- For your burstiness, Dedicated + autoscaling/burst capacity is the reliable way to maintain P99 SLAs without overpaying on hosted per-token costs.

SLA and procurement notes:
- We have SLA tiers (standard 99.9% / premium 99.95+) and optional 24x7 incident escalation for enterprise customers — Connor will share a pricing attachment and draft terms.
- VPC networking is supported for Dedicated (private egress options). If you need an on-prem or air-gapped model later, we can discuss Redwood Private but it’s usually a later-phase conversation.

Proposed next steps:
1) Connor — can you share a ballpark pricing matrix (hosted vs 1-year dedicated commit vs 3-year commit) and the SLA tier breakdown?
2) Alex/Sana — if you can give us a simple sample payload (json) and an expected request size, we’ll build a short benchmark plan and estimate the infra needed for the 3.5–5k burst window.
3) If procurement needs a doc, I’ve attached the SOW draft for Dedicated to start contract conversations.

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call this week to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
